c.tagline: The golden heart of Burgundy, serving Gothic spires, world-class wine, and its namesake mustard.

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis are metered; ranks at the train station and Place Darcy, or call ahead as street hailing is uncommon

emergency.note: 112 works EU-wide for any emergency and reliably connects to English-speaking dispatchers

avoid.reason: The Grésilles quarter has a rougher reputation after dark, and pickpockets work the station area; otherwise usual awareness.

hood_desc: Dijon's dense, largely pedestrianized old town, built around the Palace of the Dukes of Burgundy and threaded by the Owl's Trail (Parcours de la Chouette). Gothic and Renaissance mansions, the Notre-Dame church, and the covered market Les Halles are all within a short walk.

Once the quarter of wine merchants and boatmen along the Ouche canal, now Dijon's liveliest area for bars, small restaurants, and a lively Saturday market. It retains a rougher, more bohemian edge than the polished old town nearby.
A modern commercial district anchored by the Toison d'Or shopping center, one of the region's largest malls. Mostly of interest for chain shopping and a multiplex cinema rather than sightseeing.
A quiet, largely residential neighborhood northwest of the center, popular with families for its parks and easy tram access. Few tourist sights, but a good gauge of everyday Dijon life.

The university and science-campus district on the city's eastern edge, home to student housing, the botanical Jardin des Sciences, and Dijon's stadium. Quiet outside term time, livelier when students are in session.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout the city.

transit.pay: DiviaPass card, contactless bank card tap-in, or tickets via the Divia Mobilités app
transit.note: The DIVIA network includes two tram lines (T1, T2) plus extensive bus routes covering greater Dijon

train: Dijon-Ville station: TGV to Paris Gare de Lyon (~1h40), Lyon (~1h40), and Marseille
bus: Flixbus and regional coaches to Lyon, Paris, and other Burgundy towns

airport.name: Paris (CDG/Orly) or Lyon–Saint Exupéry (LYS)
airport.drive: 2.5-3 hours by car, or 1h40 by TGV from Paris

tip.r: Service is included in listed prices (service compris); rounding up or leaving small change is a nice gesture, not required
